title: XENIA FIRE DEPARTMENT
full_story:
On Saturday at 5:27 pm, the Xenia Fire Department was dispatched to a report of a structure fire in the area of Redwood Lane.

While en route, Chief 501 observed visible flames from the structure approximately one mile from the scene and immediately requested mutual aid from the North Clay Fire Protection District for additional manpower and a tanker.

Upon arrival, crews located an open-sided pole barn fully involved, with flames reaching approximately 30 to 40 feet into the air.  Nearby exposures included a tractor, a pickup truck, a fuel tank, a detached garage, and a residential structure.  The residential structure and garage were located approximately 75 feet from the fully involved pole barn.

Fire crews quickly deployed handlines and positioned themselves between the burning structure and the nearby exposures.  Through quick action and coordinated firefighting efforts, crews were able to bring the fire under control and prevent the fire from spreading.

The Xenia Fire Protection District responded with one engine, one tanker, one brush truck, and 12 firefighters.  North Clay Fire Protection District assisted with a tanker, an equipment truck, and several firefighters.

Crews were successful in protecting the residential structure and detached garage.  A tractor and pickup truck sustained minor heat damage due to their proximity to the fire.  At this time, the cause of the fire has been determined to be electrical in nature.

title: REDUCED RATE LABS
full_story:
Clay County Hospital and Medical Clinics will be hosting their popular “Reduced Rate Lab Fair” beginning April 15th through April 30th.  You may at any time pick up a voucher at the Clay County Hospital, or at the Flora, Louisville or Clay City Clinics during regular business hours.

The blood draws must be completed April 15th through April 30th.  The hours for the blood draws are Monday – Friday, 7 am – 7 pm and Saturdays from 7 am -11 am at the Clay County Hospital.  Please complete your voucher before registering.  Payment is due at registration.

Regular blood tests are an essential part of your preventative health care plan.  Multiple choices of labs are available for you to select on the voucher. The popular “Lab Fair Panel” results include the kidney and liver functions, complete blood count, and measure cholesterol levels and triglycerides.  Clay County Hospital and Medical Clinics thanks you for choosing them as your choice of healthcare and they look forward to serving you during the “Reduced Rate Lab Fair” April 15th through April 30th.

title: MARCH 17th BALLOT
full_story:
Clay County voters will head to the polls March 17th for the state’s Primary Election, with major statewide and local offices on the ballot.  Several competitive races will determine who advances to November, while others will effectively decide the next officeholder because no opponent is running in the General Election.

Republican ballots will feature 6 Choices for Dick Durbin’s senate seat, and 4 candidates including Clay County farmer Darren Bailey for governor.  For the County Board there is a race for District 8, voters, they will choose between John Bayler, Jonathan Piperakis and Rod Franklin.  For Judge of the circuit there are 4 choices, Clay County States Attorney Phillip Givens, Aaron Jones, Wesley Gozia and Brenda Mathis.

Democratic Ballots will feature 10 people running for Dick Durbin’s senate seat and 4 choices for Comptroller.

All voters will decide if the sale of retail alcoholic liquor be prohibited in Larkinsburg Township, there is also a Clay County special tax for highway purposes question, and a question to opt into the federal program that would provide public K – 12 private school, and homeschool students with privately donated funds.

full_story:

title: MILES OF SMILES COMING
full_story:
North Clay School District will be hosting Miles of Smiles on Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday.  Miles of Smiles, Ltd. is providing preventative dental services at North Clay to eligible children in all grades.

Services may include an exam/screening by a licensed dentist or licensed and certified public health dental hygienist, a cleaning, fluoride varnish application, and sealant placement if needed.  This also satisfies the dental requirement mandated by the State of Illinois for school children for Kindergarten, 2nd, 6th, and 9th grades.  There is no cost to the family or the school district.  After the services are performed, the following entities will be billed where applicable: IL Medicaid Program, public/private grants, or private dental insurance.

Miles of Smiles, Ltd. will accept any reimbursement as the final payment, even if the claim is denied.  The families and the schools are never billed for any copayments, deductibles, or balances.

Parents should fill out the printed form or scan the QR Code on the Miles of Smiles flyer.  Then create an account, provide child’s name, sign and save a copy of the form.  For more information call Miles of Smiles at 309-382-6405 or call the school at 618-665-3101.

title: JOHNSONVILLE KINDERGARTEN REGISTRATION
full_story:
Kindergarten registration for Johnsonville School will be held on Thursday from 3:30-5:30 pm.  Registration is for all students who will be entering kindergarten in the fall at Johnsonville School.  In order to enroll in kindergarten, a child must be five years old by September 1st.  Parents are asked to please bring a certified copy of your child’s birth certificate, from the courthouse, and your child’s social security number.  Immunization records, eye exam, dental exam and verification of lead screening are all necessary by the first day of school.

The registration will consist of processing the child’s paperwork and meeting the kindergarten teacher.  The school nurse will also be available to talk to parents.  In order to cut down on waiting time, please call the school office at 618-673-3044 to make an appointment to register your child for kindergarten.

The North Wayne Schools will also be conducting Child Find/Preschool Screenings for children up to 5-years in age, not yet enrolled in public schools and who will not be Kindergarten eligible in the fall.  The screening checks each child’s progress in hearing, vision, speech, language, and coordination skills.  This will give parents a better idea of how their child is progressing at this very young age before he or she begins school.  This screening program is free, and parents will receive immediate feedback on how their child is developing.  Head Start personnel may also be present to explain their program and services.

The Child Find/Preschool Screening will be held at the Johnsonville School on Monday, April 20th from 8:30 am to 2:30 pm.  The screening procedure takes about 45 minutes, and appointments must be made so that children don’t have a long wait period.  Parents should call 618-673-3044 to make an appointment or to get more information.

The service is a free check of your child’s progress in the development areas, but appointments are needed.  If you live in the North Wayne School District call 618-673-3044 today to make an appointment for your preschooler.

title: WEATHER SPOTTER CLASS
full_story:
With spring storm season ahead, the National Weather Service has scheduled a weather spotter training class in Effingham tomorrow.

The course is free and open to anyone, but only people age 18 and older will be considered storm spotters.  Topics covered during the course include severe weather hazards, safety concerns, planning for severe weather, general thunderstorm structure and movement, and how to identify important storm features.  The class will last approximately two hours, according to the NWS.

The NWS said you don’t have to live in the county where the course is being offered to attend.  The class tomorrow will be held at the County Emergency Operations Center, at 311 W Miracle Avenue, and start at 6:30 pm.
